run.character: Captain Dunstan Hobbes: a retired city guard captain with a bad knee, a good sword and no patience for gentlemen
run.persona: A classic D&D player: you investigate methodically, talk to everyone, follow the clues, and when you know who did it you go and confront them, sword ready. You enjoy a good fight with the villain.

path: Start: lane behind the King's Granary (morning). act look, sheet, then act talk_kell.

Scene 'The Hanged Clerk' (granary yard, 14 says). I examined the body: 'His stockinged feet hang well above your reach. The satchel is empty; the spectacles lie bent in the gutter.' I caught Moll's lie ('I saw him jump... At midnight. By moonlight.' in the drizzle). A silver coin got her to say a 'gentleman... Silver-topped cane. Wheat-ear ring' paid her 'a crown to say I'd seen Prout jump'. Kell linked that to 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor' and told me Prout had asked her 'how a clerk reports false entries in the King's rolls'. A second Persuasion try, with Kell's notebook put away, got Cob to describe 'Silvertop' and a 'Big bloke with a bandaged hand' in the loft after midnight, and to say he saw Prout 'sew something into one of them'. In the left boot I found the page: wagons 'lost to goblins', countersigned J. Sallow. The bandaged henchman showed up for the page, and I got him on his knees (Intimidation failed, then passed). Kell arrested him. Scene ended: 'The case is made'.

Explore (now night): lane, market square, palace gate (dead end: guards say 'you have no business'), market square, river stairs (the Drowned Rat is mentioned but can't be entered), wharves. I went there only because the prompt said 'The story is heading for The Heron Warehouse, at the wharves.'

act approach_heron, then scene 'The Heron Warehouse' (7 says). From cover I watched palace wheat-ear sacks being slit and poured into heron-stamped sacks. I got inside as a porter for Hep's gang. I saw Scrope's 'fat green ledger with a brass clasp' with every entry initialled J.S. and failed to turn him (Persuasion 5 vs DC 14), but he let slip 'Not with the Master coming'. My knee buckled (Athletics 12 vs DC 16) just as the midnight bell rang. I threw off my cloak, called 'KING'S BUSINESS!', and Sallow came in with the Crake brothers and drew a blade from his cane. I attacked, then 'Roll for initiative!'
Combat stand-in: my only action was 'fight', settled in one line: 'the Crakes are down and Sallow drops his sword-cane and asks, very politely, to surrender.'

In the same output: long rest, level up to fighter 4 (ASI +2 STR picked for me), then scene 'The King's Morning' in the King's dressing room (3 says). I gave my report and the King ordered Sallow 'held here for the Assizes'. The Crown paid the children's breakfast and a door that locks, and the Watch Captain and the Purveyor are to answer later. Scene 'Done right by', then The End.
report.solved_it: Yes, completely. Wendell Prout was murdered after midnight in the granary loft by J. Sallow ('Silvertop', who signs 'for the Royal Purveyor') and a big henchman with a bandaged hand. They wanted the page Prout had taken, hanged him off the sack hoist and barred the loft from inside so it would look like suicide. In the morning Sallow paid Moll a wheat-ear crown to say she saw him jump. The motive: Prout had found false entries. Grain wagons were written off as 'lost to goblins' while the palace grain was really being re-bagged into heron sacks at the Heron warehouse and sent away by barge. Prout sewed the proof into his boot, and Cob had taken the boots off the body. I faced Sallow at the Heron at midnight, sword drawn, and he surrendered after a fight the game settled in one line. Then I reported to the King, who had Sallow held for the Assizes. One thing stays open: the game never says whether the bandaged man I arrested was one of the 'Crake brothers'.
report.summary: I played Captain Dunstan Hobbes (human fighter 3, Champion) as a methodical guard captain and reached The End in 41 commands, 24 of them in-scene says. The first scene, The Hanged Clerk, is excellent. It is a well-laid clue chain and you can solve it with ordinary policing: the kid's oversized boots ('No boots, see? Dead men don't need 'em'), a coached lie that falls apart on the weather, a coin that gets to the truth, and a page sewn into a boot. Each NPC has its own voice: Kell is dry ('you have the King's word. It is not a warrant'; 'Noted, and nearly thanks'), Cob talks about himself as 'Cob', and Moll is prickly. The Pratchett tone works ('a watchman asleep upright against a lamppost, which is a skill'; 'The surgeon can unwrap one of them. The dead one won't object.'). Dice are shown openly, the DCs felt fair, and a different approach was allowed a retry. The Heron scene builds tension well: going in as a porter, the green ledger, my bad knee giving way (a nice use of the persona's flaw), the midnight bell, and the sword-cane. The weak points: 1. Nothing in the story leads you to the Heron. Only the meta line 'The story is heading for...' sends you there. 2. The climactic fight is a one-line stand-in with no choices or rolls, and Sallow never says a word after it. 3. The fight output runs straight through a rest, a level-up and the King's audience, so there is no aftermath. 4. There are several continuity slips: morning jumps to night, Prout is both taken down and still hanging, lavender is mentioned before it exists, and NPCs are named before I could know them. 5. The sheet's numbers look wrong, with attack bonus +2 too high and speed 35 for a human. The ending is warm and lands well: the tea callback, the children's promise kept, Kell's record saying 'murder'.
api_issues: Combat is a placeholder. The game says '(Tactical combat on the map isn't wired in yet: this stand-in resolves the fight in one go.)', the only action is 'fight', and the result is one sentence with no initiative, attack rolls, damage or HP changes. That placeholder note prints twice in the act output and twice in observe.

'act fight' runs the fight, a long rest, a level-up and the opening of the next scene ('The King's Morning') together in one output. I never got an explore or scene beat afterwards to take the ledger, check on Scrope or Kell, question Sallow, or deal with Hep's gang.
Level-up choices are made for the player: 'Choices: Ability Score Improvement; +2 to one ability score; Strength.' I wasn't asked about a feat or a different ability.
'act look' prints the room description twice: once as the look result, then again inside the full observation.

Things mentioned in explore mode can't be used. The Drowned Rat's 'light and noise' on the river stairs, the sweepers, the sleeping watchman in the market square and the palace guards have no actions. The palace gate is a dead end ('the guards make it clear that you have no business'), even though the King personally commissioned me.
Location lines read badly: 'You are in the palace gate', 'You are in the river stairs', 'You are in the wharves'.
There's no journal or clues command to review what I've learned, and no way to see my companion (Kell) or evidence I've handed over (the page is 'in Kell's notebook').

The sheet doesn't list class features or feats (Second Wind, Action Surge, fighting style, Improved Critical, origin feat), so I couldn't check the odd numbers on it. 'Heroic Inspiration' appears under Conditions after the rest, but no command lets me use it.

Some check labels name the GM's goal rather than what I said. I asked the clerk who J.S. was and where he was, and the check was labelled 'Persuasion check to persuade the clerk to give up his ledger'.
The 'The story is heading for X' line is what actually steers the player between scenes. It helps a blind tester, but it stands in for a lead inside the story.
story_issues: Nothing in the story leads you to the Heron Warehouse. Scene 1 ends with Kell saying 'Master Sallow will be at the Assembly, or in the Purveyor's offices at the palace', and nobody mentions the wharves, a barge or the Heron. I went only because the explore prompt said 'The story is heading for The Heron Warehouse, at the wharves.' A clue in scene 1 should point there, e.g. a heron stamp on the page, or Cob saying the Purveyor's wagons go down to the river.

The climax is skipped. After a strong build-up ('A narrow length of steel slides from its silver head.', 'Regrettably, the wharves are dangerous at night.'), the fight is 'after a short, ugly fight the Crakes are down and Sallow drops his sword-cane and asks, very politely, to surrender.' He never says another word. No confession, no gloating, no bargaining. Everything I learned about the 'why' came from the page and from Kell, never from the villain.

The big man with the bandaged hand, arrested at the granary, is never connected to 'the Crake brothers' who come in with Sallow at the Heron, and he isn't mentioned at the end. So the game never settles who actually put the rope on Prout.
Short overall: two investigation scenes plus the King's audience. The explore leg in between (five moves) has nothing to do.

Loose threads left hanging: Prout's empty satchel and bent spectacles, what happens to Hep's gang ('left to the watch'), and the Royal Purveyor's part in it, which the King defers ('Not in this room, and not before the Assembly'). The last two are acceptable, but the satchel should have mattered.

Positive: the boots clue is seeded early and pays off (Kell's glance at Cob's boots → 'I saw Mister Prout sew something into one of them'). The tea motif comes back in the last line, and my promise to the children is kept by the Crown in the ending.
rules_issues: The attack bonus looks 2 too high. At level 3 with STR 17 (+3) and proficiency +2, the sheet shows 'Longsword +7 (1d8+3 slashing)' where I'd expect +5. At level 4 with STR 19 (+4) it shows '+8 (1d8+4)' where I'd expect +6. The handaxe and unarmed strike are off by the same amount. It looks like proficiency counted twice, or the ranged-only Archery bonus applied to melee.
'Speed 35 ft' for a human, which is 30 ft under both the 2014 and 2024 rules. It's also odd for a character written with 'a bad knee'.
'Initiative +2' with DEX 10 (+0). That only works if he has the Alert feat (a 2024 origin feat), and the sheet lists no feats.
'Roll for initiative!' is printed twice, but no initiative or attack rolls are ever shown, and HP never drops. Nothing of D&D combat is visible to the player.
The level-up ASI (+2 STR) was picked automatically, and the player was never offered a feat.
Heroic Inspiration shows up after the long rest (2024 Human Resourceful), but there's no way to spend it.

Positive: the out-of-combat checks felt fair and fitted the fiction. Insight DC 13 against Moll; Persuasion DC 12 against a frightened child (failed on a 2, passed after I changed approach); Persuasion DC 14 against a terrified clerk; Intimidation DC 16 (failed 15, then passed 18 once my sword point was at his belly); Athletics DC 16 carrying sacks on a bad knee.
consistency_issues: Unexplained time jump. The Hanged Clerk is a morning scene, and right after it the game says 'You are in the lane behind the King's Granary (night).' Nothing describes the day passing.

The end of scene 1 contradicts itself in one output: 'She orders the constables to take him and Prout to the watch-house', then a few lines later 'Prout hangs above the yard as the Assembly bunting stirs beyond the wall.'

Constables turn up out of nowhere at the end of scene 1 to take the prisoner, though none were there before. At the Heron, Kell says 'Constables are at the Assembly route... not waiting around the corner.'

Lavender is mentioned before it exists. Watching the Heron, the text says 'No cane, no lavender, no sign of Sallow', though lavender had never come up. Only later: 'The land door opens on lavender.' It reads like the GM's private notes leaking.
NPCs are named before my character could know them: 'Hep' (the overseer), 'Scrope' (the clerk), 'the Crake brothers'.

The King reacts 'At "the cord"', but I never said 'cord' (I said 'strung him off the sack hoist'). The ending says the King 'remembers your tea order', but I never gave one. I only said I'd drink one the way Prout took his.
The bandaged henchman arrested in scene 1 and the two Crake brothers with Sallow in scene 2 are never reconciled.
Minor: the granary lane at night has 'pigeons argue in it' (the elm).
report.best_moment: The boots reveal in The Hanged Clerk. Early on Cob says 'No boots, see? Dead men don't need 'em' while 'Kell's eyes flick to the oversized boots on his feet'. Once I'd earned his trust (after a failed roll, by sending Kell's notebook away and promising 'a hot breakfast... and a door that locks'), he admitted 'I saw Mister Prout sew something into one of them, two nights before.' I searched the linings: 'In the left, your fingers find a stiff fold sewn beneath the lining. It crackles faintly when you draw it free.' It was the page of wagons 'lost to goblins' countersigned J. Sallow. Straight away: 'At the yard gate, a broad man with a bandaged hand has stopped... "Master Sallow will want that page back," he says. Cob goes white.' The clue was planted, I earned it, and it hit at once. Kell's follow-up, 'Captain, you have the King's word. It is not a warrant', was a great touch.
report.worst_moment: The fight with the villain. The Heron scene built to it perfectly: my cover blown, Sallow saying 'Captain Hobbes. How very inconvenient.', the sword drawn from his cane, the Crakes closing in, Kell coming through the door. Then the only action was 'fight' and the whole thing was one sentence: 'after a short, ugly fight the Crakes are down and Sallow drops his sword-cane and asks, very politely, to surrender.' In the same output I was taken through a long rest and a level-up and put in the King's dressing room. I never got to land a blow I chose, question Sallow, or secure the ledger. For a player who 'enjoys a good fight with the villain', that is the big letdown. A close second: going to the Heron at all was driven by the meta signpost, not by any clue.

run.character: Miss Philippa Thorne: a young court wizard, terribly well read, who is certain that every mystery can be solved with the right spell and a strong cup of tea
run.persona: A clever, curious player who uses spells to investigate (detect things, charm people, illusions), explores the town between scenes, and tries things the game might not expect. You care about getting the right answer, not just a fight.

path: Lane behind the King's Granary (morning): look, sheet, talk_kell

Scene 1 'The Hanged Clerk' (granary yard and loft, 15 say turns): stopped Cob stoning the body; ritual Detect Magic found no magic; door barred inside with the rope tied off inside; Prout shoeless and Cob in his boots; Moll's 'I saw him jump. At midnight. Moon was out' lie (it rained all night); Prestidigitation to win Cob over (Persuasion failed); followed Cob through the gap behind the water butt; in the loft found a smashed lantern, a heel streak through spilled ink, and a page cut from the Roll beside 'lost to goblins' wagon entries countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor'; Message to Cob gave 'Silvertop and the big cove'; lowered the body and found a skull swelling, a level cord mark under the noose and clean palms; Detect Thoughts on Moll gave 'Don't let Sallow know'; Kell named Master Josiah Sallow; Locate Object on the missing page; the scene ended 'The case is made' and jumped to evening

Explore (evening): lane, look; market square, look (bread price up); palace gate (turned away; say refused with 'You're not in a scene'); market square; river stairs; wharves (saw the heron-sign warehouse, which has no action); river stairs

Scene 2 'The Drowned Rat' (about 45 turns, spanning the Rat, the wharf and the inside of the Heron warehouse): read the rules board; bought gossip by the measure from Nan ('Saltmere barges load there by night'); Message plus Persuasion 17 made Big Hobb Mallory confess; found Prout's page in the left toe of Cob's boot; Find Familiar (rat Pemberton); planned the Heron infiltration with Hobb's brass heron token; trying to use the familiar's senses re-cast Find Familiar and lost an hour; a Mage Hand splash and a Prestidigitation stink hid us from Saul and the dog Duchess; Sallow arrived at midnight with the Crake brothers; Message to Hobb through the wall to cause a distraction; public accusation (natural 1); Mage Hand released a hoist sack onto a Crake; Hobb confessed publicly; Detect Magic on Sallow (nothing); a natural 20 Persuasion got the second Crake to step aside; went back in after Kell's 'unless we catch him in the act'; matched a sack's chalk tally to Prout's page; Scrope's ledger showed a 'condemned stock - sale to Saltmere factor' order written that night; Kell arrested Sallow for receiving stolen royal goods; cane surrendered; signed message to the Marshal; Hobb sheltered at Nan's; scene ended 'An ending of their own'
Long rest, level up to wizard 4 (+2 Intelligence chosen automatically)

Scene 3 'The King's Morning' (3 turns): made Prout's tea (milk first, one sugar, cup warmed) with Prestidigitation; handed over the page and gave the full report; pleaded for Hobb; asked how Sallow came to be on the procession list; ended 'Done right by', The End
report.solved_it: Yes, fully, with no combat. Who: Master Josiah Sallow ('Silvertop'), under-purveyor for grain. He struck Wendell Prout on the back of the head with his silver-topped cane, then strangled him with a cord in the granary loft. His porter Big Hobb Mallory ('kept saying Yes, Master') held Prout and hauled him up the hoist with a load-knot to fake a suicide. When: the rainy night before the story opens. Moll's 'midnight, moon was out' was a bought lie. Why: Prout found false entries in the King's Granary Roll. Royal grain wagons that Sallow had signed off as 'lost to goblins' were really being sold to a 'Saltmere factor' through the Heron warehouse for 'heron-marked' silver. Prout cut the page out to report it 'through proper channels' and hid it in the toe of his boot, which the street boy Cob then took; Sallow never found it. I faced Sallow at the Heron at midnight. Once I matched a spilled sack's chalk tally to Prout's page and the clerk Scrope admitted 'The sack count is true. The sale is not', Sergeant Kell arrested him in the act. The King had Marshal Holt hold him for the Assizes.
report.summary: This was a strong, fair detective story that rewarded evidence-based play. Every clue was physical and consistent and pointed at the same man: the door barred from inside, the rope tied off inside, the heel streak through the ink, the page cut from the Roll, a level cord mark under a slanting noose burn, clean palms, a dead man's boots on a street boy, and a moonlit sighting on a night of rain. The cast had distinct comic voices: Cob in the third person ('Cob knows what a clerk is', 'Bum-faced palace pigeon!'), Nan's 'my duck' and her gossip sold 'by the measure', Kell's deadpan 'Noted'. The game also took an unexpected route well: I never fought anyone and still ended the story properly, through Mage Hand tricks, Message whispers, matching the sack tally to the page and the honest ledger clerk. The King's closing line, 'Milk first, one sugar. You remembered.', landed. The problems were mechanical and continuity ones. The GM lost track of where people and objects were: Kell, the familiar Pemberton, Hobb and the brass token each contradicted themselves within a turn or two. Message was narrated as private, yet NPCs reacted to what was whispered. The spell layer misread intent: using the familiar's senses re-cast Find Familiar, costing a slot and an hour and making Hobb miss his bell; an explicit 'spend a slot' Detect Magic became a ten-minute ritual; Locate Object pointed away from the boy who actually had the page. Scene 2 ran about 45 turns, and the GM kept raising procedural blockers ('no warrant', 'palace is shut', 'can't hold him there') before letting it close. Exploring the town between scenes was flavor only: five locations, and the only non-movement action was the one that opened the story scene.
api_issues: `say` in explore mode fails with 'You're not in a scene: pick an action instead.' (clear), but explore mode offers almost nothing beyond moving. The palace gate guards, the Heron warehouse ('a tall tarred warehouse has a painted heron on its sign') and the granary yard after scene 1 had no actions. For an agent-QAable map, each location needs a few non-movement actions (e.g. talk_guards, approach_heron, read_bread_board).
The `look` action prints the location description twice: once as the look result, then again inside the full observation.
Location template grammar: 'You are in the palace gate', 'You are in the river stairs', 'You are in the wharves'.
In scene mode `observe` shows the recent transcript (useful), but its hint reads 'qa say --session <id> "..."' with a literal <id>, while act and say output print the real session id.
In a scene, `observe` doesn't say who is present, where the player is (the Rat, the wharf or inside the Heron, all one scene) or the in-game time; I had to infer all of that from prose.

Spell expiry notices arrive late and out of context: '🎲 Locate Object has run out' printed at the start of The Drowned Rat in the evening (cast that morning); '🎲 Detect Magic has run out' appeared several turns after I said I let it go.

Dice-line targets are odd: 'Cast Prestidigitation (cantrip) on Cob, Wendell Prout's body'; 'Cast Message (cantrip) on Big Hobb Mallory, you'; 'Cast Locate Object (2nd-level slot) on the Royal Granary Roll' when I was locating the page cut out of it.

Dice line and narration disagree: '🎲 Cast Detect Magic (as a ritual: ten minutes, no slot)' while the narration said 'spending a first-level spell slot'. The sheet confirmed no slot was spent (1st 3/4 before and after).

`sheet` doesn't track anything gained in play. No coins are listed, yet Nan 'takes your coins' four times. Prout's page, the brass heron token and the familiar Pemberton never appear. There is no inventory command.

The free-text action parser mapped 'use the telepathic bond that Find Familiar already gives me' to re-casting Find Familiar. The first try was refused with '(That isn't a spell Miss Philippa Thorne has ready: #sheet shows what they have.)' even though Find Familiar is on the sheet; the second try re-cast it, burning a slot and an hour.
story_issues: Scene 1 ended while I was following my own lead. Locate Object was pulling me toward the page ('The page is still close, but you cannot reach it from here') when it cut to 'Scene ends: The case is made', and the next observation was eight or so hours later ('(evening)') with no transition.

The King commissioned me, yet the palace gate turns his court wizard away all day: 'Nobody without business gets in on the eve of the Assembly, and the guards make it clear that you have no business.' The gating is obvious and contradicts my role.
Moll's thread never pays off. She clutches a 'crown' showing a wheat-ear and lies for someone ('Don't let Sallow know'), but who paid her and why is never resolved, and she simply runs off.

Sallow's leather folio ('private correspondence of the Royal Purveyor's office') and Captain Bunce ('Captain Bunce will hear of this before you reach the palace') are set up as threads, but neither the King nor anyone else picks them up. The procession-list oddity is waved off: 'I don't know why he was on the procession list.'

The Heron climax dragged. After Kell's arrest the GM raised one procedural blocker after another: 'I won't pretend that gives me a warrant', 'The palace is shut tonight', 'I can't hold him there for the Marshal', 'I won't sign that I witnessed Prout's murder'. That was about 20 turns from confrontation to scene end.

'The Drowned Rat' scene quietly became the whole Heron infiltration and climax: one scene of about 45 turns across three places. Its end label, 'An ending of their own', is opaque to the player; it isn't clear whether a planned fight scene was skipped.

There was little real danger. Two big Crake brothers, a gang, a dog and a murderer never threw a punch, and the one Crake I dropped a sack on stayed 'pinned' under it for many minutes. That suited my talk-first style, but the 'real stakes' never bit.
rules_issues: Message is broken as a private spell. The narration says 'the words themselves are audible only to Cob', then Moll shouts 'Cob! Shut it!' and Kell asks 'Who is Silvertop, investigator?'. Next turn, after I whispered about the page by Message, Kell asks 'The page, investigator. What page?'

Familiar sense-sharing, a core part of Find Familiar, isn't supported. Trying it re-cast the spell: '🎲 Cast Find Familiar (1st-level slot) ... The spell's work takes an hour ... The eleventh bell has passed', which made Hobb miss the deadline he had warned about.

An explicit request was overridden. 'I spend a slot and cast Detect Magic at once' became '🎲 Cast Detect Magic (as a ritual: ten minutes, no slot)' in the middle of a standoff, with the narration admitting 'Ten minutes is a long time in a warehouse'.

Find Familiar's ritual is labelled '(as a ritual: ten minutes, no slot)' while the narration says 'For an hour'. RAW is 1 hour plus 10 minutes for the ritual, and the 10 gp of components was never checked.

Locate Object gave a false direction: 'through the granary, beyond the yard doors' and 'The pull leads past the grain stacks—Cob stays hidden—then points beyond the locked doors'. The page was in the left toe of the boot Cob was wearing behind those stacks.

Detect Thoughts came with a redundant skill roll: '🎲 Insight check to get the truth out of Moll: 1 + 1 = 2 vs DC 13: failure (natural 1!)' alongside the spell. Surface thoughts were still given, so the roll was meaningless and confusing.

Arcana checks were rolled to cast the Mage Hand cantrip ('Arcana check: 14 + 5 = 19 vs DC 13', 'Arcana check: 16 + 5 = 21 vs DC 16'). Casting a cantrip shouldn't need a check; if it's meant as a precision check, the label should say so.
A contrived check: '🎲 Athletics check: 9 - 1 = 8 vs DC 16: failure', just to walk back through a door ('your foot slips on spilled grain at the threshold').

Check labels leak GM knowledge: 'Persuasion check to get Cob to trust you with what he heard' (reveals Cob heard something before he admitted it) and 'Persuasion check to get Big Hobb to tell you what he did'.

Character build: an 'Evoker' with no evocation spells and no attack cantrip; the only attacks are a quarterstaff at +1 and a dagger at +3. The persona's charm and illusion play (Charm Person, Minor Illusion) was impossible.

The level 4 level-up added no new cantrip and no new spellbook spells (wizards gain two spells per level and a fourth cantrip at level 4). The Ability Score Improvement was chosen for me ('+2 to one ability score; Intelligence').
Currency isn't tracked: I paid Nan four times with coins the sheet says I don't have.
consistency_issues: Kell is in two places at once: 'Kell steps inside, careful on the stair' (the yard doors are padlocked and the gap is 'made for a child'), then in the same reply 'Kell catches his head as you ask' on the cobbles, then next turn 'Kell looks up from the loft doorway.'

Pemberton teleports. 'At the door, Hobb looks back once, then slips out alone. Pemberton disappears into his hood.' Next turn on the wharf: 'The familiar remains on your shoulder' and 'Hobb stands a few feet away'. Later 'Pemberton is still on your shoulder' right after I put him in Hobb's hood again.

The brass token flip-flops: 'The brass heron token is no longer on the table; it is with you.' then 'you've left the brass token with Hobb' while Kell warns he'd 'arrive without the token'. Hobb's hand also later 'closes around the greasy string at his neck' after he had laid the token on the table.
The bell runs backwards: 'The eleventh bell has passed; the night loading is underway.' then next turn 'Far downriver, the eleventh bell finishes its last reverberation.'

Kell's legal stance flips: 'Master Sallow, you are under arrest for the murder of Wendell Prout.' then next turn 'I won't pretend that gives me a warrant', then 'we can't make a lawful arrest of a Purveyor's officer without a warrant unless we catch him in the act.'
Crake 2 'steps away from the doorway. He hurries to the fallen man', then two turns later 'the standing Crake abandons the doorway to move between you and his master.'
Sallow is taken 'into custody for the watch-house' overnight, but in the morning Holt says 'The Purveyor's party is formed. Sallow walks fourth.'
The King knows about 'The boot,' ('You found it there?') before I mention it.
Locate Object's direction is contradicted by where the page actually was (Cob's boot).
'Beside you, Pemberton remains hidden in Hobb's hood, quiet among the warehouse sounds beyond the closed grille' says the rat is beside me and inside the warehouse in the same sentence.
Minor: 'Prout's feet are bare, his stockinged toes turning above you.'
report.best_moment: The evidence chain at the Heron. Kell refused to act without a warrant 'unless we catch him in the act'. I knelt by the sack I'd dropped with Mage Hand and found 'a surviving chalk tally matches one of the wagon entries on Prout's page. The grain itself is clean and pale, not condemned sweepings.' Then the clerk in the counting-box defied Sallow ('The book is here, sir. I'm not bringing it down.') and confirmed the fraud: 'That order was written in this book tonight. The sack count is true. The sale is not.' Kell made the arrest. The game let careful reasoning, not a fight, beat the villain. Close runners-up: Cob's whisper back through Message ('Silvertop and the big cove... Then the thump'), finding the page ('The left toe... Something crackles in there when Cob stamps. Could be paper. Could be old socks.'), and the King's closing 'Milk first, one sugar. You remembered.'
report.worst_moment: The familiar fiasco on the wharf. I asked to see through Pemberton's eyes and got '(That isn't a spell Miss Philippa Thorne has ready)', with Pemberton (whom I'd put in Hobb's hood) back on my shoulder and Hobb (who had left ahead of us) standing beside me. I tried again, naming the existing Find Familiar bond, and the engine re-cast the spell for a 1st-level slot and an hour, so 'The eleventh bell has passed', the exact deadline Hobb had warned would tip off Sallow. The next turn then said I'd 'left the brass token with Hobb' after it had said the token 'is with you'. Three turns went to untangling state instead of playing.
